title: One exception shape for the API
summary: Register an exception handler for a domain failure and test that clients receive a stable 409 body.

scenario.briefing: A duplicate item name escapes as an unhandled exception, so the client receives a 500 with a traceback and cannot tell a conflict from a server failure. Give the domain error a stable response and test it.

objectives.description: Map a domain exception to a stable JSON response.
Test the status and body of the failure contract.
Choose the failure cases an integration suite needs.

hints: A domain exception is not an HTTPException until a handler maps it.
Return a JSONResponse with status 409 and a stable code.
Test both the status and the JSON body.

misconceptions.description: Letting a domain exception escape as a 500.
misconceptions.testDescription: A domain failure has its own exception handler.
misconceptions.feedback: FastAPI only knows HTTPException. Register a handler for the domain type so the failure becomes a deliberate response.

misconceptions.description: Putting the exception repr or traceback in the response.
misconceptions.testDescription: The response does not leak the exception text.
misconceptions.feedback: Expose a stable code and the fields the client needs. Log the detail on the server instead of serializing it.

misconceptions.testDescription: The handler returns 409 with a stable code.
misconceptions.feedback: A duplicate is a conflict with current state, so 409 is the accurate status. 500 means the server could not handle a valid request.

misconceptions.description: Locking the test to the old 500 behavior.
misconceptions.feedback: The test should assert the contract the API promises: 409 and the stable body.

misconceptions.description: Treating a 500 as an acceptable duplicate response.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Selecting the case that expects a 500 for a duplicate item.
misconceptions.feedback: A duplicate is an expected domain outcome. It must be tested as 409, not as an internal failure.

sections.title: Domain errors need a translation
sections.body: FastAPI turns HTTPException into a response, but a custom exception such as DuplicateItem has no default mapping. Without a handler it escapes and becomes a 500. @app.exception_handler(DuplicateItem) registers the translation and runs before the generic server error path.

sections.title: The body is part of the contract
sections.body: A stable code lets clients branch without parsing prose. Return JSONResponse with status 409 and a small body such as {"code": "item_exists", "name": ...}. Keep tracebacks and driver messages in server logs.

sections.title: Test the failure path on purpose
sections.body: A TestClient test should send the duplicate payload, assert 409, and compare the JSON body. raise_server_exceptions defaults to true, so an unhandled exception fails the test instead of silently becoming a response.

A failure type that describes a business rule, not an HTTP concern.
The 409 status used when a request conflicts with current resource state.
A machine-readable string that identifies a failure without exposing internals.

steps.title: Map the duplicate to a conflict
steps.prompt: Edit main.py. Register an exception handler for DuplicateItem that returns 409 with a stable code and the item name, and keep the route raising the domain error.
hints: Return status 409 with a code and the name.
Do not include str(exception) or a traceback.

tests.description: A domain failure has its own exception handler.
The handler returns 409 with a stable code.
The route raises the domain error.
The response does not leak the exception text.

steps.title: Assert the conflict contract
steps.prompt: Edit test_main.py. Assert that a duplicate item returns 409 and the exact stable JSON body.
hints: Post the same payload the handler raises on.
Change the expected status from 500 to 409.
Use the code item_exists and the submitted name.

files.content:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from main import app

client = TestClient(app)


def test_duplicate_item_returns_conflict() -> None:
    # TODO: assert the stable failure contract
    response = client.post("/items", json={"name": "Microscope"})
    assert response.status_code == 500

cases.label: Posting a duplicate name returns 409 with code item_exists.
The conflict body contains no traceback or exception string.
Posting a body with no name still returns 422.
Every exception becomes a 200 so clients never see failures.

steps.explanation: The suite must pin the expected 409 contract, prove internals are not exposed, and keep the existing validation behavior. A 500 or a blanket 200 would lock in the bug.
